scenario.narrative:
At lunch a few days ago, she was sitting near a group of eighth graders who were whisper-laughing while scrolling on their phones. She heard bits of it—comments like “that body is insane,” “she’s got the perfect shape,” and “that’s why grown men be obsessed”—and she recognized a couple names from music and Instagram. She didn’t say anything at the table, but she felt confused and a little embarrassed that she didn’t understand what they meant, especially because they spoke like it was obvious.

Later that night, she’s in an online group chat where some older kids post celebrity clips and screenshots. People keep using words like “curvy,” “thick,” “hourglass,” “snatched waist,” and “built,” and she notices the conversation keeps circling around the same parts of celebrities’ bodies, like their figure and proportions, instead of their songs or acting. She scrolls through comments and sees adults writing things like “that’s the ideal body type” and “no wonder everyone stares,” and she starts wondering what exactly makes those body types “attractive” to adults.

She opens a chat box to ask directly, trying to keep it casual so she doesn’t look babyish. She types that she overheard older kids talking about why certain famous women’s body types are “so attractive,” and asks what adults mean when they say a celebrity has the “perfect shape,” and what features they’re focusing on when they talk like that.
